hero.title: Get your time back. I build the software that runs the busywork for you.

problems.title: Start with what's slowing you down.
problems.intro: Most people come to me with one of three problems. Tell me which one sounds like you — I'll show you what I'd do about it.
problems.aiAsideLead: Not sure AI is even worth it for you?
problems.aiAsideLink: Ask me — I'll be straight with you.

busywork.title: Take the busywork off my plate
busywork.description: The repetitive admin that eats your week — invoices, follow-ups, data copied between tools — handled by software, so your hours go back to your customers.

getFound.title: Help customers find and choose me
getFound.description: A website that actually brings in enquiries and gets picked up by Google and AI assistants — designed, written, hosted, and kept current by one person.

custom.title: Build me something custom
custom.description: A web app or system built properly around how you work — fast, documented, and yours to keep, with someone technical steering it all the way to launch.

howItWorks.title: Simple, and no surprises.
howItWorks.intro: Three steps from your first message to a working result.

steps.title: We talk
steps.description: You tell me what you're trying to do, in plain words. I ask a few questions and tell you honestly whether I'm the right person to help.

steps.title: You get a fixed quote
steps.description: A clear scope and a clear price before anything starts — usually with options, so you pick what fits your budget. No hidden line items.

steps.title: I build it
steps.description: You deal with the person writing the code, so decisions are quick. You stay in the loop, and the finished work is yours to keep — no lock-in.

items.q: Do I need to understand any of the tech?
items.a: No — that's my job. I explain things in plain language, tell you what matters and what doesn't, and never hide behind jargon.
My standard rate is €120/hour, but most work is quoted as a fixed price for the scope — with options — so you know the number before we start.

items.q: What if I want changes later?
items.a: Changes are a normal conversation, not a surprise charge. Everything's built on clean, documented foundations, so later changes stay cheap.
No. The work is yours to keep — the code, the accounts, and the documentation. If we ever part ways, you or another developer can pick it straight up.
Within a day or two — with a few questions or, if it's a fit, a way forward. No hard sell.

services.title: Software and AI, delivered by the person who builds it.
services.intro: From a single landing page to the AI infrastructure behind your whole operation. Pick what fits and I'll prefill it on the form — so I know exactly what you need.

geo.title: GEO optimisation
geo.description: Get found inside AI answers, not just search results. I structure your content and data so ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity cite you when your customers ask.
geo.example: Reworked a SaaS site's content and schema so it started turning up in AI answers for its core buying questions.

landingPages.title: Landing pages, fully serviced
landingPages.description: Design, copywriting, hosting, and maintenance in one pair of hands. A fast, on-brand page that converts — and stays current without you chasing anyone.
landingPages.example: Designed, wrote, and now host a product launch page — one point of contact for copy tweaks and uptime.

automation.title: AI & non-AI automation
automation.description: Hand the repetitive work to software. I connect your tools and automate the boring steps — with AI where it earns its place, plain code where it doesn't.
automation.example: Automated invoice intake and follow-ups for a small firm, saving roughly half a day of admin each week.

aiInfrastructure.title: AI business infrastructure
aiInfrastructure.description: The foundation that makes AI useful across your business — knowledge bases, retrieval, and the plumbing that keeps models grounded in your own data.
aiInfrastructure.example: Built a private knowledge base and retrieval layer so a team's assistant answers from their docs instead of guessing.

aiConsultancy.title: AI consultancy
aiConsultancy.description: A straight second opinion on where AI fits — and where it doesn't. We find the few use cases worth doing and skip the hype that burns budget.
aiConsultancy.example: Reviewed a startup's AI roadmap and trimmed it to the two features that actually moved the numbers.

projectManagement.title: Project management
projectManagement.description: Someone technical to keep a build on track — scope, timelines, and contractors coordinated, with honest status you can act on.
projectManagement.example: Ran delivery on a multi-vendor web build, keeping scope and timeline aligned all the way to launch.

software.title: Software engineering
software.description: Web apps and systems built to last: fast, accessible, documented, and easy to change. Clean architecture today means cheap changes tomorrow.
software.example: Shipped a custom client portal on clean, documented architecture the team can extend themselves.

leadGen.title: Lead-gen channel development
leadGen.description: Build the channels that bring work in — referral systems, outreach, and the tooling behind them — so growth isn't only word of mouth.
leadGen.example: Set up a referral and outreach system that gave a consultant a repeatable source of new enquiries.

about.p1: I'm Jamie Nisbet, a software engineer and AI consultant based in {location}. I've spent years building for the web, and I now design AI systems built to run for the long term — documented and built to scale, not demos that break a month later.
about.p2: I work as a small shop on purpose. You deal with the person writing the code, so decisions are quick and nothing gets lost in translation. For bigger builds I bring in trusted contractors — you keep the responsiveness and gain the capacity. If something's a bad idea, I'll tell you.
